## Purpose

`mlmr` provides a free, reproducible, HLM-style graphical workflow for
multilevel modeling in R. Users, instructors, and reviewers should be able to
inspect both the supported feature matrix and the deterministic validation
benchmarks that protect core workflows against regressions.

## HLM-Style Feature Parity

`mlmr` covers the core teaching and publication workflows expected from
level-based multilevel software while keeping every step grounded in `lme4`:

```{r parity, eval = TRUE}
knitr::kable(mlmr::mlm_hlm8_parity())
```

## Deterministic Validation Benchmarks

`mlmr` ships eight deterministic benchmark specifications covering two-level
null, random-intercept, random-slope, cross-level interaction, three-level
nested, cross-classified, longitudinal growth, and binary logistic GLMM
workflows.

By default (`run = FALSE`), `mlm_validation_benchmarks()` checks expected
formulas and model-readiness guardrails without fitting models:

```{r benchmarks, eval = TRUE}
knitr::kable(mlmr::mlm_validation_benchmarks(run = FALSE)[, c(
  "Benchmark", "Expected Formula", "Formula Match", "Readiness Stops", "Validation Status"
)])
```

## Fitted Benchmark & Round-Trip Code Verification

When `run = TRUE`, `mlm_validation_benchmarks()` fits all eight benchmark
models and verifies:

- AIC agreement against stored reference values;
- fixed-effect point estimates and standard errors;
- random-intercept variance components and Gaussian ICCs;
- automated round-trip execution of the exported R script (`Repro Code Match`)
  in an isolated R environment to confirm that exported code reproduces the
  exact fitted coefficients.

```{r fit-benchmarks, eval = FALSE}
mlmr::mlm_validation_benchmarks(run = TRUE)
```

## Reviewer-Facing Validation Report

To generate a complete multi-table validation object from R or download it from
the **About** tab of the Shiny app:

```{r validation-report, eval = FALSE}
report <- mlmr::mlm_validation_report()
names(report)
```

The report bundles benchmark status, fixed effects, variance components, ICCs,
Nakagawa $R^2$, and convergence diagnostics across all eight reference models.
